label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
**Written Statement Regarding Complaint of October 29**

To: Mrs. Okafor
Copy: Darlene [Last Name], Supervisor, Transportation Office, for driver file
From: [Your Full Name], Driver, Bus 41, Route 9 Elementary
Date: [Date you sign it]
Regarding: Afternoon drop-off, Tuesday, October 27, Kessler Ave and Brandt St stop

Dear Mrs. Okafor,

My supervisor gave me a copy of your complaint on November 3, and I was asked to write down my account of what happened on the afternoon of October 27. I know this statement goes in my file and that you will get a copy. I'd like to talk to you directly as well as to the office, since you are Amara's mother and I am the one who drives her every day.

First, I want you to know I understand how scared you must have been. I have grandchildren of my own. If I were waiting for one of them and watched the bus pull away with them still on it, I would have been frightened and upset too. I am sorry you had that kind of afternoon. I mean that.

I also want to explain exactly what I saw and why I did what I did, so you have the whole picture.

**What happened at the stop**

On Tuesday, October 27, I was driving Bus 41 on the Route 9 elementary afternoon run. Amara's stop is at Kessler Ave and Brandt St. The schedule time for that stop is 3:50. I got there at 3:52.

Amara has the green tag on her backpack. On our route the green tag means an adult has to be at the stop to meet the child before I can let them off. Like all kindergarten riders, Amara falls under that rule.

When I pulled up, I looked for an adult at the corner and did not see anyone. I waited until about 3:55 and kept watching the corner and the sidewalk on both sides of the bus. I still did not see anyone there for Amara.

I understand you have said you were parked across Brandt St near the laundromat and that you waved. I believe you were there. But I did not see you. A box truck was parked on that side of the street, and from the driver's seat it blocked a good part of my view of that side. I was not ignoring you. If I had seen you, I would have done everything I could to get Amara to you safely.

**Why I could not get off the bus to look**

I know it may seem like I could have stepped off and looked across the road. When I was at your stop I still had 14 children on the bus and three more stops to make. I cannot leave a bus full of children unattended to cross a street and look around. That is not something I am allowed to do, and in 28 years I never have. My job at that moment was to keep every child on that bus safe, and that includes Amara.

**What the policy says and what I did**

The district rule for kindergarten riders is clear. If no adult is at the stop, the child stays on the bus and goes back to the school, and the office calls the parent. I followed that rule.

At 3:56 I radioed dispatch. Gloria at dispatch took the call and contacted Fairmont Elementary to let them know Amara was coming back and that the parent needed to be reached. I finished my last three stops and dropped off the rest of the children.

I got Amara back to Fairmont at 4:31. I did not just let her off at the curb. I walked her into the office myself and handed her over to Mrs. Petrakis.

**How Amara was doing**

I want you to know Amara was fine the whole time. She was not upset or crying. She sat in her seat and colored on her folder. At one point she asked me if she could ride some more. I told her we were going on a little extra trip, and she was happy with that. I kept it calm and easy for her on purpose. I did not want her to be scared.

**About the comment that I "drove off laughing"**

I understand the office was told I drove off laughing. I was not laughing. As we pulled away from the stop, a fourth grader in seat 2 had stood up, and I was telling him to sit back down. I may have been talking or turned toward him, and I can see how that could look like something else from across the street. But nothing about that afternoon was funny to me, and I would never laugh at a parent who was worried about her child.

**Request to review the bus camera footage**

Bus 41 has a camera system. I am respectfully asking the transportation office to pull the footage from October 27 covering the Kessler Ave and Brandt St stop, from my arrival at about 3:52 until I pulled away, and the ride back to Fairmont. I believe it will show that I stopped, waited, and looked for an adult, and that I was dealing with the student in seat 2 when we pulled out. It should also show how Amara was doing on the bus. I think the footage will help both Mrs. Okafor and the office see what I saw.

**A request to help this not happen again**

Mrs. Okafor, I would like this to go better for both of us from here on. The stop is the most important part of my day with Amara, and I want you and me to be able to see each other clearly.

If it is possible, I would ask that you wait on the same side of the street as the bus, at the corner, so I can see you as I pull up. If you need to stay in your car across the street, could you please step out of the car where I can see you? With parked trucks and traffic on that side of Brandt, a wave from inside a car is very hard to catch from the driver's seat. Once I see you, I can let Amara off right away.

If there is ever a day you are running late or something comes up, calling the school or the transportation office ahead of time helps too, so they can let dispatch know.

**Closing**

I have been driving for 28 years and have never had a write-up. Something like this has happened only once before on my route, years ago, with a different family. After it was explained, they thanked me, because they understood the rule is there to protect their child. I am not saying that to compare you to anyone. I only want you to know I take this seriously and that I do it the same way for every child.

I will not apologize for following the rule, because that rule exists to keep kindergartners safe, and Amara's safety comes first for me. But I am sincerely sorry you were scared and that your afternoon went the way it did. I would never want a parent to feel that way.

I am glad to keep driving Amara. She is a sweet girl and a pleasure to have on the bus. I hope we can work this out and get back to good, easy afternoons at the Kessler and Brandt stop. If you would like to talk about it, I would be glad to sit down with you and Darlene.

Respectfully,

______________________________
[Your Full Name]
Driver, Bus 41, Route 9 Elementary
[Employee ID number, if your office uses one]

Date: ____________________

---

A couple of things before you turn it in Friday:

- Fill in your name, Darlene's last name, and your employee number if they use one.
- If your district handbook has a section number for the kindergarten drop-off rule, you can add it after the "What the policy says" heading, something like "(Transportation Policy section __)." It isn't required, but it makes the record stronger.
- Keep a copy for yourself, and ask Darlene to note the date she received it.
